scope: Curated primary-source literature and documentary benchmark; supports the sole DDS

sources.author: NIST
sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.access: Selected full text: risk context; MEASURE2.1–2.6; MANAGE2.1
sources.use: Deployment conditions, traceable measures, residual risk and viable alternatives. Supports contextual evaluation; does not prescribe DDS or validate its results.

sources.author: NIST
sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.access: Selected full text: MS-2.5-001/002 and human-AI configuration
sources.use: Use generalizability limits and document human contribution. Narrow demonstrations cannot establish broad capability. A risk profile is not a comparative test result.

sources.author: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Introduction to AI assurance
sources.access: Selected official full text: toolkit, proportionality, certification example
sources.use: Distinguishes assurance techniques and supports proportionate selection. DDS can produce evidence for a wider assurance process; citing this guidance does not make DDS an accredited certification scheme.

sources.author: ISO
sources.title: ISO 31000:2018 — Risk management — Guidelines
sources.access: Official catalogue/abstract; normative text not reviewed
sources.use: Provides a general risk-management reference beyond AI. Use as contextual terminology, not a claim of clause-level conformity.

sources.author: ISO and IEC
sources.title: ISO/IEC 23894:2023 — Artificial intelligence — Guidance on risk management
sources.access: Official abstract; normative text not reviewed
sources.use: Connects AI risk management to organizational activities. An alignment map needs licensed/full clauses and specific evidence before any conformity claim.

sources.author: ISO and IEC
sources.title: ISO/IEC 25059:2023 — Quality model for AI systems
sources.access: Official abstract/status; normative text not reviewed
sources.use: Useful quality vocabulary and completeness questions. Catalogue flags a forthcoming replacement; the cited2023 edition must be pinned and refreshed for commissioned use.

sources.author: Leveson, Nancy G. and Thomas, John P.
sources.title: STPA Handbook
sources.access: Selected full text: purpose/losses, control structure, unsafe actions, causal scenarios
sources.use: Established system/human hazard analysis and feedback discipline. Use it to generate or challenge scenarios; an authored finite STPA exercise is not full industrial STPA validation.

sources.author: SCSC Assurance Case Working Group
sources.title: Goal Structuring Notation Community Standard (Version3)
sources.access: Official citation/abstract; PDF access blocked in this review
sources.use: Supports explicit engineering argument structure. Metadata confirms scope/version only; no clause-level or notation-conformance claim is made from the inaccessible body.

sources.author: Object Management Group
sources.title: Structured Assurance Case Metamodel (SACM), version2.3
sources.access: Selected full text: scope/context, argumentation and artifact provenance
sources.use: Connect claims, arguments, assumptions and evidence. Provides an established assurance-case substrate; DDS does not automatically conform to the metamodel.

sources.author: Lamport, Leslie
sources.title: Specifying Systems: The TLA+ Language and Tools for Hardware and Software Engineers
sources.access: Author preliminary draft; selected sections8.9.4 and composition
sources.use: Formal preservation/implementation reasoning supports carefully directed transfers. A source analogy or passed fixture cannot replace the applicable proof obligations.

sources.author: Lamport, Leslie and Merz, Stephan
sources.title: Prophecy Made Simple
sources.access: Selected full text: section3 implementation/refinement mappings
sources.use: A concrete refinement mapping establishes a directed implementation relation. Use to distinguish implication from full isomorphism; DDS/R01 proofs remain separately owned.

sources.author: NIST and SEMATECH
sources.title: e-Handbook of Statistical Methods — Choosing an experimental design; randomized block designs
sources.access: Official sections5.3 and5.3.3.2
sources.use: Blocking and randomization help control nuisance variation in executed comparisons. Apply only when the scoped empirical design warrants it; no universal factorial grid is required.

sources.author: Liang, Percy and others
sources.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM)
sources.access: Author methodology;2023 TMLR citation checked in official repository
sources.use: Coverage, incompleteness and multiple metrics are established evaluation principles. Software entered maintenance mode in2026; framework merit and current maintenance are distinct.

sources.author: Kapoor, Sayash and Stroebl, Benedikt and Siegel, Zachary S. and Nadgir, Nitya and Narayanan, Arvind
sources.title: AI Agents That Matter
sources.access: Selected full text: cost, downstream needs, shortcuts, reproducibility
sources.use: Control cost and task definition; avoid benchmark shortcuts and weak holdouts. Supports simpler strong baselines and honest deployment transfer.

sources.author: Kapoor, Sayash and others
sources.title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
sources.access: Author abstract; official HAL description and ICLR2026 citation
sources.use: Existing standardized agent harness, cost-aware comparison and trace inspection deserve full credit. A common harness still needs a deployment-specific question and valid scoring.

sources.author: Rabanser, Stephan and Kapoor, Sayash and Kirgis, Peter and Liu, Kangheng and Utpala, Saiteja and Narayanan, Arvind
sources.title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
sources.access: ICML2026 publisher abstract; official reliability documentation
sources.use: Separates consistency, robustness, predictability and safety. DDS should consume applicable reliability evidence rather than claim these dimensions are new.

sources.author: Yao, Shunyu and others
sources.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.access: Selected full text; ICLR2025 publication;2024 preprint
sources.use: State-based scoring, domain policies and repeated-run pass^k. A simulated user is not human-capacity calibration; pass^k and pass@k answer different questions.

sources.author: Barres, Victor and Dong, Honghua and Ray, Soham and Si, Xujie and Narasimhan, Karthik R.
sources.title: tau2-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
sources.access: ICML2026 publisher abstract; current official repository notes
sources.use: Shared agent/user actuation and ablation are existing benchmark capabilities. User simulation does not establish actual human readiness, authority or workload.

sources.author: Debenedetti, Edoardo and others
sources.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
sources.access: Author abstract and release-change note
sources.use: Tool tasks over untrusted data evaluate task utility alongside injection resistance. Relevant to security controls; broader non-adversarial deployment adequacy requires its own scope.

sources.author: SWE-bench team
sources.title: SWE-bench Verified
sources.access: Official project/dataset description:500 human-filtered instances
sources.use: Executable software-repair tasks supply meaningful outcome verification. A coding benchmark result is not general evidence of oversight or business value.

sources.author: METR
sources.title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
sources.access: Official methodology/FAQ; Time Horizon1.1 selected
sources.use: Human-expert task duration indexes difficulty at a stated success level. It is not the agent's wall-clock duration or the human escalation response window.

sources.author: UK AI Security Institute
sources.title: Inspect AI — evaluation framework and scoring policy
sources.access: Official framework/scoring/sandbox documentation
sources.use: Custom tasks, logs and scoring distinguish evaluated failure from instrument failure and unscored samples. Good execution infrastructure; a harness does not decide the substantive research question.

sources.author: Mitchell, Margaret and others
sources.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
sources.access: Author abstract and FAT*2019 venue metadata
sources.use: Documents intended use, evaluation and limitations. Reuse available cards as sources; documentation does not itself demonstrate deployment fitness.

sources.author: Gebru, Timnit and others
sources.title: Datasheets for Datasets
sources.access: Author abstract; CACM2021 publication metadata
sources.use: Data motivation, collection, composition and intended use help qualify fixture/source evidence. A datasheet is not a proof that a dataset represents a deployment.

sources.author: NASA
sources.title: NASA Task Load Index (TLX)
sources.access: Official instrument description
sources.use: Subjective multidimensional workload measurement can inform a human study. It does not establish competence, authorization, decision accuracy or empirical HID.

sources.author: SPIFFE project
sources.title: SPIFFE Overview
sources.access: Official specification overview
sources.use: Workload identities and authentication are conventional capabilities. Identity validity alone does not establish claim truth, current authority or timely human intervention.

sources.author: Birkholz, H. and Thaler, D. and Richardson, M. and Smith, N. and Pan, W.
sources.title: RFC9334 — Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Architecture
sources.access: Selected full text: roles, appraisal policies, freshness; Informational RFC
sources.use: Attester/verifier/relying-party separation and freshness qualify state evidence. A local JWS fixture is not native device attestation or full RATS conformance.

sources.author: Burrows, Mike
sources.title: The Chubby lock service for loosely-coupled distributed systems
sources.access: OSDI2006 full text: section2.4 sequencers
sources.use: Resource-side sequencer checks reject stale lock use. A strong conventional baseline should receive credit; a generation token without enforcement is insufficient.

sources.author: Amazon Web Services
sources.title: The confused deputy problem — IAM User Guide
sources.access: Official cross-account/cross-service documentation
sources.use: Established scoped-delegation safeguards include trust-policy external IDs. Evaluate the actual configured native policy; identity-only failure does not show a competent IAM baseline fails.

sources.author: HM Treasury
sources.title: The Green Book: UK government guidance on appraisal
sources.access: Selected official full text: objectives/options, uncertainty and switching values
sources.use: Comparing options and material assumptions helps qualify value claims. Transfer the appraisal principle proportionately; DDS is not a complete public-sector appraisal or universal ROI calculation.

sources.author: BSI
sources.title: AI Performance Assessment — Independent AI verification
sources.access: Official service description; provider claims, no purchased assessment
sources.use: Documented independent performance/fairness/reliability assessment and recognition. Credit this established assurance offering; its mark and DDS Sponsor recognition have different meanings.

sources.author: Giskard
sources.title: AI Agent Evaluation — Giskard Hub
sources.access: Official product/workflow docs; no hands-on product benchmark
sources.use: Custom checks, local/remote/scheduled evaluation and version comparison overlap DDS execution needs. Continuous testing is a documented product strength.

sources.author: Cisco
sources.title: Introducing Agent Harness Testing in Cisco AI Defense
sources.access: Official release description; no hands-on product benchmark
sources.use: Tool routes, indirect content and persistent agent state are documented testing surfaces. DDS cannot claim agent-harness evaluation is an unoccupied market.

sources.author: Holistic AI
sources.title: AI Audits — Mitigate and Monitor AI Risks
sources.access: Official service description; no purchased audit
sources.use: Sociotechnical risk assessments, context-specific reporting and mitigations are established service offerings. Scope and independence need engagement-specific evidence.
